item.title: Seeking Greenlight: SCP idea: Re: Seeking Greenlight: SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
Hello Galcedion! let's take a look :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: A dead space ship from the future, which has an invisible entity on board that can kill in atmospheric environment and is sentient.

Considering the skip is capable communication, and sounds (at least to extent) self aware. I'd say sapient is the better way to describe the skips intelligence/awarness.

The narrative:

Central Narrative: The SCP is divided into 2 parts, the ship (SCP-XXXX) and the entity (SCP-XXXX-1). The ship is an advanced human design (not Foundation) that at the current time should not exist. The crew has been killed either by the entity or during venting atmosphere (attempt to kill the entity by the captain). One of the Foundation researchers notes a couple of things about the ship including a device that appears to allow travelling through spacetime using another dimension. Also there is one body missing.

The entity was not on the ship when it engaged its device. It either came from the travel-dimension or said dimension altered a crew member (or both). It can be heard walking around the ship and is pretty harmless in void. It can jump between ships and when in any atmosphere, arms may come from the walls, pulling people "inside" the walls and killing them in the process (they are basically split into their atoms). This is an attempt to pull people into its "dimension", hinted to be an communication attempt.

The Foundation team sent to explore the ship finds the original crew dead, some melted to the ships structure. After a while a team member is killed by the entity (accident with suit leads to air escaping) and more die during the escape due to friendly fire and a hull breach. 2 survive and try to communicate with the entity (that can understand visual things like guestures but not writing) while they slowly run out of oxygen and there is no help coming soon.

For the most part, I second cybersqyd here. The narrative did interest me at first, however it turned into a murder story (and a rather cliched one) before anything in the concept could really be explained or expanded upon.- currently this sort of reminds me of alien.

As it stands, the main questions the concept raised are still here (i.e the ships original purpose, the skips initial motives ect.) which makes the narrative feel a bit anti-climactic and unfinished, as there's no real payoff or buildup to anything major.

Another thing I should mention; How do you plan to show all of this info being learned in the narrative? Currently, a lot of this info sounds unobtainable by the Foundation (i.e the skip is only dangerous in the atmosphere, the ship is from the future, the skip wanting to communicate ect.), as there isn't much of a method to learn about the skip or understand and communicate with it (at least not one the Foundation could realistically learn with no prior knowledge of the skip).

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight.

-I would recommend expanding more on the initial questions raised in the concept more, through the narrative. Rather than just turning the narrative into murder monster story with no context or wider explanation. Give something that links everything together, perhaps the skip was part of the reason the ship was here to begin with? maybe the crew were trying to send a warning of some sort? ect.

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques/perspectives in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

RED

item.title: @fterlife.net (seeking greenlights): Re: @fterlife.net (seeking greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Sorry writer, but you need a specific layout for the Ideas Critique Forum in order for it to be accepted.

Seeking Greenlights: Put yes or no.

Page Type: SCP Article, Tale, GoI Format, Joke SCP, Site Dossier, Other (specify)

Genre (Optional): Horror, Drama/Emotional, Comedy, Action, History, Other (specify)

Page Layout (Optional): How will you structure the page in terms of information presentation, or plot development? If you plan on using a unique format/format screw, describe that here.

Elevator Pitch: What is the basic core idea? Use a bullet point list if necessary.

Central Narrative: Describe the story beats or overarching context/"big picture" for your piece. If there is no story content, put "none". (Note that it is extremely rare for articles without narrative context or worldbuilding content to receive greenlights.)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: What is novel/unique about your premise? What is special about your idea here that will make it stand out among the other works already on the mainsite?

Additional Notes: Note any concerns or particular areas of assistance you would like reviewers to focus on.

item.title: any suggestions for my SCP?: Re: any suggestions for my SCP?
item.content:encoded:
I'm not really a fan of the central narrative section; it feels…too expected and too focussed on the backstory of this. My general advice when writing a SCP is to forget about why it exists (and how the Foundation found it, a little). In general, backstory is not the most interesting angle because it happens a) before the foundation get involved (and so, before any of the PoV characters can be there) and b) it's just, not very interesting; and this suffers from this a lot since there's not really any way for the Foundation to know about the mans' gradual discovery of his powers, not a lot happens while he discovers them, and it's very temporally removed from the here and now and the people involved in the story.

item.title: SCP "Darkhouse" - [Seeking Greenlight]: SCP "Darkhouse" - [Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Terminal / SCP Historical

Page Layout (Optional): Discovery (audio recordings; scanned original documents; terminal)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Perhaps there was a reason why the O5-Council decided to bury this information…

Elevator Pitch:
+ Open
- Close

A Junior Researcher logs onto an older terminal and uncovers a forgotten SCP with deep roots in the SCP foundations history.


Central Narrative:
+ Open
- Close

The SCP foundation has a questionable history, but this Junior Researcher attempts to solidify one of the oldest SCPs discovered by the Foundation. Compiling information from older terminals and transcribing paper archives, the SCP “Darkhouse” is reclassified as one of the earliest discovered SCPs. The SCP was “lost” when the Foundation transferred their data from paper to computers.

Dating back to 1792, the original Cape Henry Lighthouse was the first federally funded public works project of the newly formed United States government. In 1881, a new lighthouse was constructed to replace the original. With rising threats from around the world, both human and anomalous, the United States government attempted to utilize unexplainable properties the original lighthouse possessed.

The SCP “Darkhouse” ‘s anomalous properties are charged by UVA (315-400 nm) and UVB (280-315 nm) Ultraviolet radiation. The radiation appears to activate the anomalous properties, causing the SCP “Darkhouse” to enter an “active” state. During this state, the SCP “Darkhouse” will project a photon-absorbing substance, blocking all light it encompasses. Effects of the substance on living organisms have been redacted due to its tendencies to dissolve and dissipate matter. Containment procedures have been automated and the SCP “Darkhouse” has not been attended to by Foundation personnel since its original containment.


Additional Notes: “It doesn’t shine, it shadows…”

item.title: Uncertain Unreality: Uncertain Unreality
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Psychological… something

Page Layout (Optional): A normal SCP article, but it's split into two distinct sections

Elevator Pitch: The SCP itself is more or less the designation for two separate scenarios. In scenario A, the SCP is a Euclid SCP, who's a young human girl, a bit distorted from reality, and makes half of the people who know of her think she doesn't actually exist.
In scenario B, the SCP is an infohazardous memetic effect, which makes half of the people who know of it think that there's a person there, who really isn't.
The memetic effect of either scenario is so powerful, and so overwhelming, that despite their best efforts, the foundation can't tell which one is true, so they've documented it as if it's neither and both at the same time.
After all, it's impossible to prove either way

Central Narrative: The main narrative is gonna come from how the scenario A SCP is mentally affected by her affliction, and how she may have gotten like this based on interviews with her and the like
Also, it's going to focus on how this uncertainty is affecting the foundation personnel who know of the SCP, including conflicts starting due to people in scenario A starting fights with people in scenario B
People are getting angry about a whole humanoid containment chamber which is going completely unused

Hook/Attention-Grabber: the main hook is obviously the esoterics of something that can't be proven to exist or not exist, and possibly how the foundation reacts to encountering something that they can't truly understand despite their best efforts. I'd imagine people would already be interested as soon as they see "Object Class: Euclid / Keter (?)"

Additional Notes: I guess above all else I want to know if this concept has been done before and if so I would like to know how to make it more unique.
Also, I just wanna know if it's good or not alltogether

item.title: Skeleton's Daycare: Skeleton's Daycare
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: I don't really know, maybe a bit emotional in some parts?

  • Elevator Pitch
  • Central Narrative
  • Hook/Attention Grabber
  • Additional Notes

It's a daycare owned by a living skeleton. The skeleton itself isn't anomalous (though it can talk, which skeletons aren't able to do, but that's about it), it's just a normal human who decomposed into a skeleton but is still alive due to some crystals on the walls.

There's no other staff in the daycare, but what they do have are alien children to take care of. For the most part, they're fairly normal. They have a bit of a temper, but that's just kids being kids. They are capable of causing minor earthquakes though, so you might not wanna anger them too badly.

This daycare used to be pretty normal. Then these alien parents came in and had to drop their kids off because "they had to do something (translation: they were being abandoned)." When they left the kids at the daycare, they left them with some crystals that would make them immortal.

Two people used to run the daycare, but the original owner left to go find the parents because they've been gone for way too long and they can't close without all the kids leaving. This left the other guy to run it all by himself, but the owner was out for so long that the other guy's body died and became a skeleton.

After some time, one of the alien parents came back and took their kid, along with one of the crystals. This caused the skeleton's life to become much harder. This, along with the stress of taking care of aliens, was adding up.

At some point, the skeleton couldn't take it anymore and just left the building, causing him to die from getting out of range from the crystals. The children were attached to him after living there for a long time, so they tried to bring him inside and get him to live again, but it didn't work. Remember in the Elevator Pitch how the kids could cause minor earthquakes? They're really upset now, and they're causing serious damage to the rest of the world. They tried calming them down, but nothing would work. Because of the danger and the fact that the parents weren't coming back, they had to neutralize them.

A daycare slowly going into ruins.

[Note from the owner: Kill me.]

item.title: Please don't stare: Please don't stare
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, History.

Page Layout (Optional): Probably a good chunk of the article will be filled with dialogues.

Elevator Pitch: a humanoid SCP cursed with a deadly beauty: anyone that makes eye contact cannot feel happiness after that, slowly losing the will to live. The physical aspect of the SCP is different for each person.

Central Narrative: This being would be discovered when the suicide rate of a small town began to show astronomic growth. When brought to the foundation site, a scientist would open the eyes and bring a curse to 5 foundation personnel. The SCP would cooperate with the foundation to try and find a solution, but no amnestics would work and the five would eventually die of starvation or commit suicide, leaving the SCP crying on the corner of it’s cell. Following this tragic event, a series of cold-hearted tests would be performed, including sending many D-class personnel to stare at it’s eyes. The O-5 council decided to shut down the tests for being “too cruel” and the tests would now only be performed in case of someone accidentally staring the creature.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Testing on the SCP would show superhuman strength and resistance, as well as high knowledge in diverse areas and an extensive vocabulary, including many different languages. The SCP would have its own personality, portrayed by the “logs” of his conversation between the scientists, and it loves someone to read a book to it. This SCP is a pacifist, knocking out the opponents instead of killing them (this would be proven in the few containment breaches of his).

Additional Notes: I hadn’t come with a cool name yet. Also, if anyone finds an existing SCP with a similar concept, please notify.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight for first SCP: True NPC: Seeking Greenlight for first SCP: True NPC
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): (meta) Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Two variants of the article, one describing the SCP upon discovery and initial tests, the other after learning about it's true scope

Elevator Pitch: Self aware NPC attempts to break out to the real world, after Foundation tries to contain it, and learns about multi-layered nature of the Foundation reality, created specifically to stop pataphysical threats

Central Narrative: Foundation learns about the existence of a self aware character from roleplaying games, whose name is a cognitohazard, that forces people perceiving it to include this character in their roleplaying activities. They try to contain it, like any other memetically spreading SCP, but it did not want to have its freedom restricted, so it decided to break out to the real world. Foundation, prepared for this kind of pataphysical dangers, created beforehand many layers of fictional realities, each identical to the top one, with Earth, Foundation and all the jazz, to contain entities traveling upwards through layers of fictional realities.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Afaik there are no skips going "upwards'' through the reality layers, besides SCP-3812, who accidently went from our reality one level higher, but we don't have any coming from "below" and on purpose. Similarly, there is a multitude of fictional (from the in-universe point of view) SCPs but not much connected to the roleplaying (books and computer games get the majority of attention in this area afaik). I'm also planning on exploring limits of the mentioned cognitohazard, and the entity itself through test logs (something I see rather rarely, but find personally fascinating).

Additional Notes: English is not my first language (as you can probably tell) and I'll be thankful for pointing any misspellings or grammar mistakes. Also I never before used any »real« internet forum more complicated than facebook or reddit, so I'm sorry in advance for my mistakes while trying to make sense of it (I hope that I created this post in the right way). Thanks for reading, I hope you will like my idea, and maybe I'll manage to get the greenlight for my first SCP ^^

item.title: The Grave Of A Chief: Re: The Grave Of A Chief
item.content:encoded:
Hi, yes Id be happy to elaborate! 400 words is a little restrictive.

The mountains were actually giants yes, the entire mountain range is the bodies of these giants who were slain in the war. And the tribes were reality benders yes but comparativley weak at it compared to other reality benders since its an aquired power and not something they have inherently like a "true" reality bender (if there even is a criteria.)

+ Show
- Close

I was unable to include it in the main post but the war was initiated by the common "betrayal of god" story of many indigenous tribes which is similar somewhat to the tower of babylon in that all animals and humans and gods used to speak a common language until humanity betrays their god(s). They often (though not in all tribes) fight a war between the animals and humans in which they always lose and are forced to migrate to what ever their home is when they tell the story.

though god in the sense its understood in indigenous stories is that they are limitless in knowledge and in creation but they are unable to control anything they create outside of outsmarting them, since self determinism itself is something thats impossible to override, even for gods. Which is why they are forced to talk to humans occassionally.

As for how the giant mythos, the betrayal of god and war tie to the tribe being able to bend reality and sacrificing it,
the tribe sacrificed their reality bending powers to keep the mountain they now call chief mountain from dying in the war that resulted from their betrayal of god. This tribe, who saved the chief mountain, are one of the few tribes who werent forced to migrate as the mountain sacrificed itself to kill the rest of the giants which is why the tribe sacrificed their reality bending to keep it alive, since they couldnt save it completely you can think of it as them keeping the mountain on life support through both the sacrifice of intial reality bending powers and continued rituals.

the mountain isnt contained by this initial sacrifice, i guess neutralized would maybe fit better but i was unsure if that would still apply if the anomoly wasnt fully neutralized and still posed a threat eventually. All the sacrifice did was keep the mountain from dying of its own sacrifice for the tribe, which was to protect them from the other giants and animals from the war.

The political gains part is that the mountain is still a strong ally of the small tribe and if you were a small group who lost a war to an empire and were gifted essentially a weapon of mass destruction, the literal power of a mountain to weild at your will. would you not become mad with power? would you not attempt to assert your power and claim your own piece of the pie? I thought it only seemed natural as every tribe in real life sees themselves as nations in conflict with whatever country they live in (US, Canada, mexico, etc) so if you have the nation vs nation mindset and got incredible power, asserting that power politically would naturally follow.

so the foundation needs to contain the mountain in one of a few ways, containing it in conjunction to the tribe, contain it without the tribes involvment at all or if nothing else killing it. This is where the political aspect comes into play again, the foundation needs to make sure the entity is contained to its area. Though they eventually realize that even if the tribe were appeased, and in the best case scenario, they werent greedy and only took a small area for their nation. The mountain itself is still autonomous so the foundation is unsure if the mountain could be kept perpetually contained by the tribes persuasion to it, as in the past humanity, and the tribes in particular, have their history of betraying their god. So they could potentially betray the mountain and cause the foundation to lose their , potentially only means of containing it
so the foundation is torn between just circumventing the tribe all together and risking expending massive resources to potentially contain something but with the benefit thay if they do, itll be perpetually. as opposed to appeassing the tribe which is a known way to contain the entity, low on resources and could buy some time, but also isnt garunteed to last forever, essentially its a bandaid solution.

Sorry if thats alot to read, i hope you better understand how everything ties together. If you still dont understand ill try to work the story into a less complex and more focused story but i wanted to be able to explain alot of the seemingly unconnected ideas that a come to form the larger arc and not just the specific story in this specific time period, i wanted to include past and future events in some capacity.

item.title: A Simple Bar: A Simple Bar
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery/Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Interview logs and also a log about when the bar manifested and when the Foundation sent an MTF in to determine if the place is a threat

Elevator Pitch: A "simple" bar and owner of said bar, that has the ability to hop across dimensions in order to serve as many customers as possible. Said bar
sets up shop just outside a Foundation site in the middle of nowhere in the hopes of making more money.

Central Narrative:
+Block
-Block

The bartender and owner is relatively open and talkative about the people he's met and places he's been, but when the foundation start trying to find out
some of the more personal questions about his and the bars history he starts getting more dismissive and less talkative. My idea is that the Owner used to run the place with his brother until they traveled to a dimension they weren't welcome in, with the consequence being that the brother is kept half dead, bloody, and basically soulless chained up in the back room of the bar. The owner is unable to let his brother die and let himself move on, so he pays the strange man who lives in the dimension a fee every month for him to help keep his brother alive. In an attempt to make as much money as he can to pay the strangers increasing demands he puts his bar down next to a very busy Foundation site. The interviews with foundation staff start fine with the owner happily telling stories and chatting, but each interview he gets more and more reserved and disturbed with hints and clues as to his brothers fate, until just before an interview the owner comes out from the backroom with blood on his hands with tears in his eyes.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: What I'm trying to go for is it starting all happy with stories and fun banter and slowly see it turn into horror.

Additional Notes: I plan on leaving most of the history of the place only hinted at so the reader could speculate and come to their own conclusions.

I guess my big concern is: what are these testing logs showing? It kinda feels like they might feel…pedestrian; but I think a few showcasing the various melodies it produces could be a fun little middle section.

The logs do showcase are variety of the melodies the chime can produce, though they are often not limited to just songs, but anything that can be considered loosely musical (such as a heart monitor or an all-clear alarm). The intention was to have a recovery log, a testing log, a long term exposure log, and a reverse engineering log. Two of those I've already written in the draft.

Uhhh what children? Are they just a some children who are enamoured by the clock or?

For some reason I didn't want to give away the entire story within the idea critique, but the shop was using foster children, for their small nimble fingers, to manufacturer the SCP. (There is also an implication that it has to be specifically orphaned children for the 'magic' to work).

The test logs feeling awkwardly inserted between the discovery section and the epilogue…

That's my bad for implying the testing logs are between the epilogue and the recovery section. They're not, they're the 2nd to last segment (the last is an audio recording of the chime).

…it might just need some kinda hint as to why the two people responsible made this and what they were intending, y'know?

I wasn't going for any outlandish intentions, the people responsible were using the anomalous nature, and the enamoring factor oft he SCP to sell it for exceptionally large amounts of money.
